activities.name: Diving Sipadan
activities.note: permit-limited: Sabah Parks issues a fixed number of dive permits each day, shared between the resorts and dive centres, so book well ahead

windows.reason: the diving season runs April to December, with vertical walls, green and hawksbill turtles and schooling barracuda

activities.name: Perhentian Islands
activities.note: the diving and snorkelling season runs March to October

windows.reason: the northeast monsoon: most resorts, ferry services and dive shops shut until the season restarts
the northeast monsoon: ferries run much less often, many places to stay close and most dive shops shut
the diving season, March to October

activities.name: Climbing Mount Kinabalu
activities.note: every summit climber needs a permit and a licensed local guide, and the mountain huts can book out months ahead

windows.reason: climbing weather is at its best around April
the rainy months; rain and mist make the summit trail more dangerous

activities.name: Thaipusam at Batu Caves
activities.note: the Hindu cave temple outside Kuala Lumpur draws thousands of devotees and onlookers

windows.reason: held on the full moon of the Tamil month of Thai, which falls in January or February

activities.name: Kaamatan harvest festival
activities.note: Sabah's harvest festival, with the Unduk Ngadau pageant, Sumazau dance and folk sports

windows.reason: celebrated through May and culminating in the public holiday on 30 and 31 May

activities.name: Gawai Dayak
activities.note: Sarawak's Dayak harvest festival, with longhouse open houses

windows.reason: the 1–2 June public holiday marks the end of the rice harvest; celebrations often run through the rest of June

activities.name: Rainforest World Music Festival
activities.note: held at the Sarawak Cultural Village at the foot of Mount Santubong, outside Kuching

windows.reason: an annual three-day festival, usually in late June or July; the dates shift each year
